newsitem.title: USA: Rhode Island eyes record $254 mln bond referendum.
newsitem.headline: Rhode Island eyes record $254 mln bond referendum.

text.p: Rhode Island's voters on Nov 5 will approve or reject a record total of approximately $254 million of bonds that have been proposed for a variety of projects, a state official said late Monday.

The bond offerings that have been placed on the ballot include $72 million for upgrading the Quonset Point abandoned naval station by improving the deepwater port and rail access, said Jim Thorsen of the Treasurer's office, who spoke here at a Bond Buyer conference on public finance in New England.

A total of around $80 million of bonds would be sold to raise money for upgrading transportation, with about $74 million going for computers at state universities and colleges and improving their physical plants.
Environmental and brownfield clean-ups would get about $9 million, with $18 million spent to upgrade state facilities, he added.

Rhode Island has about $1.7 billion of tax-supported debt but it does not see the large volume of new issues, which Thorsen said polls indicate voters likely will approve, as putting the state's finances at risk.
"Despite the additional $254 million, a lot of thought and effort has been put into how to do that and remain fiscally prudent," he said.
The state official noted that the state has been paying off so-called debt for DEPCO, which was set up to address the savings and loan bail-out, more quickly than first anticipated.

Further, Rhode Island's improving economy has bolstered tax receipts, Thorsen said, adding revenues are expected to be up $27 million, according to the latest consensus revenue forecast. While this could help produce a bigger surplus than expected, he noted that next year some taxes sunset, which could hurt revenues unless these taxes are renewed.
